scope: Task #83 local validation runner, static rules checks, safety boundaries, and local behavior evidence only.

claims.statement: The previous manual validation path used six separate validation calls; the runner exposes those checks through one fixed invocation while still executing six auditable subcommands for current-ci-equivalent.

In the Task #83 live targeted probe, the fixed runner entry executed directly as the first command in a new Codex session with project rules loaded; Guardian turns, approval prompts, and elevated executions were all zero. This observation applies only to the targeted probe and does not measure current-ci-equivalent or post-merge live Guardian behavior.

Static execpolicy checks cover allowed runner profiles plus negative cases for interpreters, shells, GitHub writes, dangerous Git operations, unknown profiles, and known injection prefixes; the Runner verifies trusted files against HEAD and rejects non-canonical command IDs/argv before subcommands execute.

Tests include bounded failing pytest, failing git diff, process-group timeout and interruption cleanup, trusted Runner/spec/Rules replacement rejection, non-canonical command rejection, CI drift, and result-write failure cases.
Task #83 does not execute Task #65 candidate and does not claim token reduction or candidate superiority.

A controlled pre-review reproduction showed that a mutable profile specification could turn an allowed runner entry into an unrelated command path. Runner 1.0.1 now verifies trusted HEAD blobs and canonical command IDs/argv before execution.

A controlled pre-review reproduction showed that direct-child-only timeout handling could leave descendants alive. Runner 1.0.1 uses bounded process-group cleanup, with regression coverage for a grandchild process.
The live Rules observation used runner 1.0.0. The unchanged Rules entry supports the routing claim, while runner 1.0.1 runtime hardening is supported by tests rather than that earlier live probe.

The fail-closed design requires synchronized updates across CI, profile spec, canonical allowlist, drift tests, Rules tests, and documentation; trusted-file changes must be committed before the fixed runner can execute.
